normalization.window_list_order: Valid window.list rows are paired by stable numeric ref and positional indices are recomputed. Every row identity and field remains strict; malformed or duplicate refs are not normalized.
normalization.reason: Both native implementations enumerate unordered window registries; dictionary iteration order is not product behavior.

categories: window.keyed cleanup ownership derived from the OS-selected fallback key
platform_equivalences.strict_guards: Responses, errors, event names/order/origins/counts, UUID/ref identity, visibility, workspace linkage, selector routing, and all non-approved fields remain strict. The non-active close case retains its active-route identity delta.

behavior: A close appends an invisible recoverable window.list row with stable window/workspace ids, refs, selection, and workspace count, including the matched CLI-created rows.
Live native rows precede recoverable rows and win identity collisions.
A failed native close discards staged history; successful close commits it atomically.
A repeated close of a committed recoverable route is idempotent and returns its stable window id/ref without another event or mutation.
Restart clears the in-process recoverable history.
closed_window_history.measurement_correction: Canonical intentionally retains closed windows as invisible recoverable routes. The previous until_absent predicate incorrectly classified this product behavior as failed cleanup. until_window_not_visible now accepts visible:false or absence while keeping the final row payload strict.
closed_window_history.result: The environment-matched 68-case pair has zero unsatisfied settles and a valid 66-equivalent/2-delta comparison after exact platform-pointer review.

residual_clusters.name: post_close_active_routing
residual_clusters.evidence: After close settles non-visible, canonical selector-less workspace.list reports the closed target (window:6/workspace:7) while Windows reports its live fallback (window:1/workspace:1). Platform path/key leaves are removed and this identity mismatch remains strict.

residual_clusters.name: last_window_close
residual_clusters.evidence: Canonical disconnects during last-window close and emits one more lifecycle event; Windows replies success without exiting. This remains a product-semantic gap or an explicit platform-equivalence decision.
